hero.title: Sandy hills, **straight stripes.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Clarkston lawns every week: mowed, trimmed, edged along every walk and curb and blown off clean. Sandy knobs, soft lake edges and tight village yards each get cut the way they need.

local.title: Lawns that **dry out on top** and stay wet below.
local.intro: Clarkston lawns sit on glacial ground. The USDA soil survey maps a lot of Independence Township as sandy, gravelly outwash, well drained and quick to dry, with muck in the hollows by the lakes and wetlands. One yard can have both, and a mower run the same way across all of it leaves ruts at the bottom and scalped spots at the top.

points.title: High spots brown first
points.body: Sandy soil holds less water than loam, MSU Extension says, so the knobs and south facing slopes go tan first in a dry July. MSU's rule is to mow around 3 inches or higher and never take more than a third of the blade at once. Taller grass shades its own soil, and that matters most up there.

points.title: Hills that need a trimmer
points.body: Some soil map units in the township run from 12 to 40 percent slope, and there is a ski hill at Pine Knob for a reason. Banks too steep for a mower deck get string trimmed instead, and if a bank is a weekly fight, Rob will say so and suggest a bed.

points.title: Lake lots
points.body: Independence Township asks lake owners to keep clippings out of the water and the street, since drains and ditches run to the lakes, and suggests a 15 foot strip of taller grass along the shore. We blow clippings back onto the lawn, and we can leave that strip long if you want it.

points.title: Village yards along the walks
points.body: In the old village around Main Street, yards are small and nearly every one fronts a sidewalk. That makes the edge line the part people notice, so walks and curbs get a crisp cut and the clippings come off the concrete before the truck leaves.

logistics.title: A set day each week, all season.
body: Your lawn gets a regular mowing day, so you know when to expect the truck and when the gate needs to be unlatched. If you have a dog, tell us. One customer's review singles out how careful the crew is about keeping the dogs in.

Each visit is the whole job: mowed, trimmed around beds and trees, edged along the drive and the village walks, and blown off. Open lawns get stripes, straight, curved or crosscut, and Rob will suggest a pattern that suits the shape of the yard.

Rob gives you the price at the estimate, before the first cut. Mowing pairs well with a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-clarkston-mi/) and [fall leaf removal](/leaf-removal-clarkston-mi/), so the lawn starts and ends the year clean.

faq.q: Who mows lawns in Clarkston, MI?
faq.a: Grand Scapes does. We mow lawns in Clarkston and the rest of Independence Township every week of the season, with trimming, edging and a blown off drive and walk on every visit. Call or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) for a free estimate.

faq.q: How often should my lawn be mowed?
faq.a: Weekly through the main growing season is the usual answer. MSU Extension's rule is to remove no more than a third of the blade per cut, and in a wet May a Clarkston lawn can outgrow that in less than a week. In a dry August, a sandy lawn slows down on its own.

faq.q: Can you mow a steep yard in Clarkston?
faq.a: Usually, yes. The hills here are real, and banks too steep for a mower get trimmed instead. If a slope is a fight every week, Rob may suggest turning it into a planted bed or holding it with a [block wall](/bed-edging-and-block-walls/).

faq.q: Do you leave the clippings on the lawn?
faq.a: Clippings that land on the grass stay there; MSU Extension says they can go back to the lawn when you cut no more than a third at a time. Whatever lands on the drive, the walk or the road gets blown back in, because Independence Township points out that its street drains lead to the lakes.

faq.q: When is the last mow of the year in Michigan?
faq.a: When the grass stops growing, which in most years is late in the fall. The last cuts often double as light leaf cleanup, since a mower chops a thin layer of leaves into the turf. A heavy layer is another story, and that is what [leaf removal in Clarkston](/leaf-removal-clarkston-mi/) is for.
